bar.name: v1 HTML fixtures and A2UI for the same apps; 300 blind English requests; independent end-to-end attack on stored rows

biggest_gap: Whether a `was` clause is already applied is inferred from per-slot rename records, and restore-to-version drops them. After a restore to a later version, or on an older backup, an unrelated edit that keeps the clauses swaps the values again while diff says safe.

acceptance.line: >= 90% of 300 blind requests expressible (programs parse and type-check)
acceptance.evidence: mo.mjs check passes on all 330 programs. Coverage of unseen requests not re-measured this round.
300 corpus programs: keyword tokenizer median 133, p90 239, max 811.

acceptance.line: every prefix cut at a line end parses
acceptance.evidence: Prefix test passes inside 533/533; fuzz-check 20,000 mutations on a fresh seed: 0 crashes, 0 grammar disagreements.

acceptance.line: edits never lose or retype saved data while marked safe
acceptance.evidence: All three round 4 repros are fixed (51k fuzz steps, 0 mismatches). New: restore to version then an edit keeping `was` flips a swap (S1); same on a backup without the new bookkeeping (S1); restore-to-version after an option rename strands rows (S2).

other_notes: S2: an old snapshot loaded with the newest program fails when a rename step was skipped, and `history` is ignored when the snapshot has `ever`. S2: repeating the same swap or rotation is a silent no-op with an empty change list.
S3: a pick option renamed without `was` is still verdict safe with only a note.
Orchestrator decision for round 6: stop inferring. Store the program without `was` once applied, keep a name-to-slot map per version, and rebuild maps for old backups by replaying version texts.
